summary: All four compliance gates cleared. Data originates exclusively from the SEC IAPD bulk download — a federal government open-data system requiring no authentication, no payment, and no API key. All 61 columns are firm-level regulatory fields; zero individual-person PII is present. Commercial resale of formatted U.S. government data is legally well-established and precedent-confirmed by AdvizorPro, FINTRX, and RIA Database operating commercially on the same source for years. No sector-specific privacy statute (GLBA, CCPA) applies because no natural-person financial data is included — every row is a registered business entity, not a consumer. Clear to ship. Two required corrections to the opportunity-brief marketing language are flagged below and MUST be applied before the engineer creates any listing copy.

public_data_source.rationale: Dataset sourced exclusively from the SEC Investment Adviser Public Disclosure (IAPD) compilation page (https://adviserinfo.sec.gov/compilation). The raw ZIP (ia050126.zip) was downloaded from https://www.sec.gov/files/investment/data/other/information-about-registered-investment-advisers-exempt-reporting-advisers/ia050126.zip — a direct U.S. federal agency server URL requiring no login, no API key, no paywall, and no rate-limiting access control. The DataGov catalog listing (https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/information-about-registered-investment-advisers-and-exempt-reporting-advisers) independently confirms public availability. The opportunity brief confirms source_rights.public = true with two corroborating URLs. Every row carries a source_url pointing to https://adviserinfo.sec.gov/compilation, satisfying the hard provenance rule. No auth-bypass, no login scraping, no purchased data — 100% clean public harvest.

pii_assessment.rationale: All 61 columns are firm-level or regulatory fields. There are no individual-person names, no personal email addresses, no Social Security Numbers, no dates of birth, no personal home addresses, and no consumer financial account data. The data-steward independently confirmed pii_check_no_email_addresses: PASS across all 16,551 rows (the 141 '@' characters found are YouTube channel handle URLs, e.g. youtube.com/@handle — not email addresses). Phone numbers are publicly disclosed business main-office lines filed with the SEC on Form ADV Part 1, not personal mobile numbers. Street addresses are registered principal office locations. AUM figures are aggregate business metrics (sum of assets under firm management), not any individual client's account balance. Client-type and employee counts are business-level aggregate statistics. has_disclosure_events and disclosure_event_count are regulatory flags sourced from public IAPD disciplinary records — not personal criminal history. This is standard B2B entity data; no field identifies or enables re-identification of a natural person.

commercial_resale_rights.rationale: Works produced by officers or employees of the U.S. federal government as part of their official duties are in the public domain under 17 U.S.C. § 105 — no copyright attaches. The SEC is a federal agency; Form ADV bulk data is a direct product of its statutory mandate under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (15 U.S.C. § 80b-4). The adviserinfo.sec.gov portal publishes under an open-data policy with no restriction on downstream commercial use. Established market precedent confirms legality: AdvizorPro, FINTRX, and RIA Database have each operated commercially on this exact same SEC source data for years without legal challenge, with AdvizorPro alone generating $5K–$20K annual contracts from 600+ financial institution clients. The SEC's own EDGAR and IAPD terms of use contain no prohibition on commercial redistribution of the data; the only restriction is against misrepresenting the SEC as a data partner (which DataStructured does not do). No terms-of-service clause on adviserinfo.sec.gov or catalog.data.gov prohibits commercial redistribution.

sector_specific_privacy.rationale: Three sector-specific statutes were evaluated: (1) GLBA (Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. § 6801 et seq.) — GLBA governs how financial institutions protect the non-public personal information of their customers. DataStructured is not a financial institution, and this dataset contains no customer non-public personal information. Every row is a registered advisory firm (a business entity), not a consumer. GLBA does not apply. (2) CCPA/CPRA (California Consumer Privacy Act) — CCPA protects 'consumers' defined as California residents acting in their personal or household capacity. B2B information about business entities and their employees acting in a professional capacity is explicitly excluded from CCPA's individual-consumer protections under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.145(o)(1). CCPA does not apply. (3) SEC Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) — governs protection of consumer financial privacy by SEC-registered entities. DataStructured is not an SEC-registered adviser; nor is this dataset derived from any client-specific financial relationship. Reg S-P does not apply.

Selling points must not claim a field the product does not contain. (b) '200+ fields' — the dataset has exactly 61 columns. The '200+ fields' figure was copied from RIA Database's own product marketing and does not describe this product.

notes: 16,551 rows validated — all status=Approved SEC registrants. 228 Pending/Inactive rows correctly excluded by data-engineer.
source_url present on 100% of rows — hard provenance requirement satisfied.

2,179 rows (13.2%) missing US state: 887 are foreign-address RIAs (Canada, Europe, Pacific territories — no US state applicable); 1,292 have no address filed with SEC. Both are source-data characteristics, not harvesting or compliance issues.
13 records with malformed phone strings (0.08%) — filed as-is with the SEC. Non-blocking.

862 firms carry has_disclosure_events=Y — this field is a legitimate public IAPD regulatory flag and a selling point for compliance/due-diligence buyers. Its presence is appropriate and adds product value.
21 ADV filings pre-dating 2024 — these are SEC-filed values for long-dormant but still-registered firms. Not a compliance issue.

The 'custodians' data referenced in the opportunity brief IS accessible in a separate IAPD Schedule D bulk extract. If the engineer wishes to add it as a future dataset enrichment or bundled bonus, that is a product decision for the CEO — it does not affect this dataset's compliance status.
